en: Ishaq ibn 'Umar ibn Salit al-Hudhali narrated to me: Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, from Thabit, who said: Anas said: I was with 'Umar; (and a different chain) Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us—and the wording is his: Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: We were with 'Umar between Makkah and Madinah and looked for the crescent moon. I was a man with sharp eyesight, so I saw it, while no one else claimed to have seen it besides me. He said: I began saying to 'Umar, "Do you not see it?" but he could not see it. He said: 'Umar said, "I will see it while lying on my bed." Then he began narrating to us about the people of Badr, saying: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, used to show us the death places of the people of Badr the day before, saying: "This will be the death place of so-and-so tomorrow, if Allah wills." 'Umar said: So by the One Who sent him with the truth, they did not exceed the boundaries that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had demarcated. He said: They were placed in a well, one on top of another. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, went until he stopped by them and said: "O so-and-so son of so-and-so, and O so-and-so son of so-and-so, have you found what Allah and His Messenger promised you to be true? For I have found what Allah promised me to be true." 'Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, how do you speak to bodies that have no souls in them?" He said: "You do not hear what I say any better than they do, except that they cannot reply anything to me."

'Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar al-Qawariri narrated to me: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us: Budayl narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Shaqiq, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "When the soul of a believer departs, two angels receive it and ascend with it." Hammad said: and he mentioned the pleasantness of its scent and mentioned musk. He said: "And the inhabitants of heaven say: 'A good soul that has come from the direction of the earth. May Allah bless you and the body you used to inhabit.' So it is taken to its Lord, Mighty and Majestic, then He says: 'Take it to the ultimate term.'" He said: "And when the soul of a disbeliever departs"—Hammad said: and he mentioned its stench and mentioned cursing—"and the inhabitants of heaven say: 'An evil soul that has come from the direction of the earth.' So it is said: 'Take it to the ultimate term.'" Abu Hurayrah said: Then the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, turned a shawl he was wearing over his nose like this.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Abu Bakr ibn Nafi' narrated to us, saying: 'Abd ar-Rahman—meaning Ibn Mahdi—narrated to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Khaythamah, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib regarding: {"Allah keeps firm those who believe, with the firm word, in this worldly life and in the Hereafter"}: He said: It was revealed concerning the torment of the grave.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar ibn 'Uthman al-'Abdi narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Alqamah ibn Marthad, from Sa'd ibn 'Ubaydah, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said regarding: {"Allah keeps firm those who believe, with the firm word"}: He said: "It was revealed concerning the punishment of the grave, when it is said to him: 'Who is your Lord?' and he says: 'My Lord is Allah and my Prophet is Muhammad, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.' That is His words, Mighty and Majestic: {'Allah keeps firm those who believe, with the firm word, in this worldly life and in the Hereafter'}."

'Amr ibn Zurarah narrated to me: 'Abd al-Wahhab—meaning Ibn 'Ata'—reported to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Prophet of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "When the servant is placed in his grave and his companions turn away from him..." and he mentioned the like of the hadith of Shayban from Qatadah.

Muhammad ibn Minhal ad-Darir narrated to us: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us: Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "When the deceased is placed in his grave, he surely hears the patter of their sandals when they depart."

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Shayban ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman narrated to us, from Qatadah: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us, saying: The Prophet of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "When the servant is placed in his grave and his companions turn away from him, he surely hears the striking of their sandals." He said: "Two angels come to him, make him sit up, and say to him: 'What did you use to say about this man?' As for the believer, he says: 'I bear witness that he is the servant of Allah and His Messenger.' It is said to him: 'Look at your seat in the Fire; Allah has exchanged it for you with a seat in Paradise.'" The Prophet of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "So he sees them both." Qatadah said: And it was mentioned to us that his grave is widened for him seventy cubits and filled with greenery until the Day they are resurrected.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us; (and a different chain) 'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: My father narrated to us; (and a different chain) Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar both narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, all of them from Shu'bah, from 'Awn ibn Abi Juhayfah; (and a different chain) Zuhayr ibn Harb, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Ibn Bashshar all narrated to me from Yahya al-Qattan—and the wording is Zuhayr's: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us: 'Awn ibn Abi Juhayfah narrated to me, from his father, from al-Bara', from Abu Ayyub, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, went out after the sun had set and heard a sound, whereupon he said: "Jews being punished in their graves."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar both narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Were it not that you would not bury one another, I would have supplicated to Allah to let you hear of the punishment of the grave."

Yahya ibn Ayyub and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah both narrated to us from Ibn 'Ulayyah; Ibn Ayyub said: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us; he said: And Sa'id al-Jurayri reported to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from Zayd ibn Thabit; Abu Sa'id said: I was not present with the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, but Zayd ibn Thabit narrated it to me, saying: While the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was in an enclosure belonging to Banu an-Najjar riding a mule of his and we were with him, it suddenly shied with him and almost threw him off. There were graves, six, five, or four—thus al-Jurayri used to say—so he said: "Who knows the occupants of these graves?" A man said: "I do." He asked: "When did these people die?" The man said: "They died in polytheism." He said: "Indeed, this nation is tested in its graves. Were it not that you would not bury one another, I would have supplicated to Allah to make you hear of the punishment of the grave that which I hear." Then he turned his face toward us and said: "Seek refuge in Allah from the punishment of the Fire." They said: "We seek refuge in Allah from the punishment of the Fire." He said: "Seek refuge in Allah from the punishment of the grave." They said: "We seek refuge in Allah from the punishment of the grave." He said: "Seek refuge in Allah from tribulations, both visible and hidden." They said: "We seek refuge in Allah from tribulations, both visible and hidden." He said: "Seek refuge in Allah from the tribulation of the Dajjal." They said: "We seek refuge in Allah from the tribulation of the Dajjal."

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: 'Abd ar-Razzaq reported to us: Ma'mar reported to us, from az-Zuhri, from Salim, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "When a person dies, his seat is shown to him morning and evening: if he is of the people of Paradise, then Paradise; and if he is of the people of the Fire, then the Fire." He said: "Then it is said: 'This is your seat to which you will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection.'"

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: I recited to Malik, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "When one of you dies, his seat is shown to him morning and evening: if he is of the people of Paradise, then from the people of Paradise; and if he is of the people of the Fire, then from the people of the Fire. It is said: 'This is your seat until Allah resurrects you to it on the Day of Resurrection.'"

Abu 'Ammar Husayn ibn Hurayth narrated to me: Al-Fadl ibn Musa narrated to us, from al-Husayn, from Matar: Qatadah narrated to me, from Mutarrif ibn 'Abdullah ibn ash-Shikhkhir, from 'Iyad ibn Himar, brother of Banu Mujashi', who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, stood among us one day delivering a sermon, and said: "Indeed, Allah commanded me..." and he related the hadith similar to the hadith of Hisham from Qatadah, and added to it: "And indeed Allah revealed to me that you should be humble so that no one boasts over another and no one oppresses another." And he said in his hadith: "and they among you are followers seeking neither family nor wealth." I said: "Does that happen, O Abu 'Abdullah?" He said: "Yes, by Allah, I met them in the pre-Islamic days of ignorance, when a man would tend the flock of a tribe having nothing to his name except that he would cohabit with their slave-girl."

'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Bishr al-'Abdi narrated to me: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Hisham—the companion of ad-Dastawa'i: Qatadah narrated to us, from Mutarrif, from 'Iyad ibn Himar, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, delivered a sermon one day... and he related the hadith, and said at its end: Yahya said: Shu'bah said, from Qatadah: "I heard Mutarrif in this hadith."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna al-'Anazi narrated it to us: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah with this chain of narration, and he did not mention in his hadith: "Every wealth I have bestowed upon a servant is lawful."

Abu Ghassan al-Misma'i, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Muhammad ibn Bashshar ibn 'Uthman narrated to me—and the wording is that of Abu Ghassan and Ibn al-Muthanna—they said: Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us: My father narrated to me, from Qatadah, from Mutarrif ibn 'Abdullah ibn ash-Shikhkhir, from 'Iyad ibn Himar al-Mujashi'i, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said one day in his sermon: "Lo, my Lord commanded me to teach you what you were ignorant of from what He taught me this day: 'Every wealth I have bestowed upon a servant is lawful. And I created all My servants as upright monotheists (hunafa'), but the devils came to them and turned them away from their religion, made unlawful for them what I had made lawful for them, and commanded them to associate with Me that for which I sent down no authority.' And Allah looked upon the people of the earth and despised them, their Arabs and non-Arabs, except remnants from the People of the Book. And He said: 'I have only sent you to test you and to test others through you; and I have sent down to you a Book that water cannot wash away, which you recite while asleep and awake.' And Allah commanded me to burn Quraysh, so I said: 'My Lord, then they will crush my head and leave it like a piece of bread.' He said: 'Drive them out just as they drove you out, campaign against them and We shall campaign for you, spend and We shall spend upon you, send an army and We shall send five like it, and fight with those who obey you against those who disobey you.' And he said: 'The people of Paradise are three: a ruler who is just, charitable, and guided; a man who is merciful and soft-hearted toward every relative and Muslim; and a chaste person who restrains himself despite having dependents.' And he said: 'The people of the Fire are five: the weak person who has no self-restraint, those who are among you as followers seeking neither family nor wealth; the dishonest person whose greed is never concealed even in petty matters except that he betrays it; a man who does not wake in the morning or reach the evening without deceiving you regarding your family and your wealth'—and he mentioned stinginess or lying—'and the foul-mouthed, obscene person.'" And Abu Ghassan did not mention in his hadith: "spend and We shall spend upon you."

Al-Hakam ibn Musa Abu Salih narrated to us: Yahya ibn Hamzah narrated to us, from 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Jabir: Sulaym ibn 'Amir narrated to me: Al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad narrated to me, saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say: "The sun will be brought near to the creation on the Day of Resurrection until it is at a distance of a mil from them." Sulaym ibn 'Amir said: "By Allah, I do not know whether by mil he meant the distance on earth or the probe used to apply kohl to the eye." He said: "Then people will be submerged in sweat according to their deeds: among them will be those whose sweat reaches their ankles, among them will be those whose sweat reaches their knees, among them will be those whose sweat reaches their loins, and among them will be those whom the sweat bridles completely." And the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, pointed with his hand to his mouth.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz—meaning Ibn Muhammad—narrated to us, from Thawr, from Abu al-Ghayth, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "On the Day of Resurrection, sweat will indeed go seventy cubits deep into the earth, and it will surely reach up to people's mouths or to their ears." Thawr doubted which of the two he said.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Musayyabi narrated to us: Anas—meaning Ibn 'Iyad—narrated to us; (and a different chain) Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to me: Hafs ibn Maysarah narrated to us, both from Musa ibn 'Uqbah; (and a different chain) Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar and 'Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Ibn 'Awn; (and a different chain) 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ma'n narrated to us: Malik narrated to us; (and a different chain) Abu Nasr at-Tammar narrated to me: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Ayyub; (and a different chain) al-Hulwani and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, from Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd: My father narrated to us, from Salih, all of them from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, with the meaning of the hadith of 'Ubaydullah from Nafi', except that in the hadith of Musa ibn 'Uqbah and Salih: "until one of them is submerged in his sweat up to halfway up his ears."

Zuhayr ibn Harb, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and 'Ubaydullah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Yahya—meaning Ibn Sa'id—narrated to us, from 'Ubaydullah: Nafi' reported to me, from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, regarding: {"The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds"}: He said: "One of them will stand in his sweat up to halfway up his ears." In the narration of Ibn al-Muthanna he said: "Mankind will stand," and did not mention "The Day".

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us; (and a different chain) Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Bahz narrated to us, both saying: Wuhayb narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn Tawus narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said: "Mankind will be gathered in three ways: hoping and fearing; two upon a camel, three upon a camel, four upon a camel, and ten upon a camel; and the Fire will gather the rest of them, staying overnight with them wherever they spend the night, taking the midday rest with them wherever they rest, being with them in the morning wherever they enter morning, and being with them in the evening wherever they enter evening."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us; (and a different chain) 'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: My father narrated to us, both from Shu'bah; (and a different chain) Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn al-Muthanna's—they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Mughirah ibn an-Nu'man, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, stood among us delivering an admonition and said: "O people, indeed you will be gathered unto Allah barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised: {'As We began the first creation, We will repeat it. A promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We will do it'}. Lo, indeed the first of creation to be clothed on the Day of Resurrection will be Ibrahim, peace be upon him. Lo, indeed some men from my nation will be brought and taken toward the left, so I will say: 'O Lord, my companions!' But it will be said: 'You do not know what innovations they introduced after you.' So I will say as the righteous servant said: {'And I was a witness over them while I remained among them; but when You took me, You were the Observer over them, and You are, over all things, Witness. If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise'}. He said: Then it will be said to me: 'They continued to turn back on their heels ever since you parted from them.'" And in the hadith of Waki' and Mu'adh: "So it will be said: 'Indeed, you do not know what innovations they introduced after you.'"

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Zuhayr ibn Harb, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us—Ishaq said: reported to us, while the others said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who heard the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, delivering a sermon saying: "Indeed, you will meet Allah walking, barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised." And Zuhayr did not mention in his hadith: "delivering a sermon."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Numayr both narrated to us: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, from Hatim ibn Abi Saghirah with this chain of narration, and he did not mention in his hadith: "uncircumcised."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Hatim ibn Abi Saghirah: Ibn Abi Mulaykah narrated to me, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'A'ishah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say: "Mankind will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, women and men all together looking at one another?" He, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "O 'A'ishah, the matter is far too severe for them to look at one another."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn Idris narrated to us; (and a different chain) Ibn Numayr narrated to us: My father and Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us; (and a different chain) Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Musa ibn A'yan reported to us; (and a different chain) Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me: Abu Usamah narrated to us, all of them from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid; (and a different chain) Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me—and the wording is his: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Isma'il narrated to us: Qays narrated to us, saying: I heard Mustawrid, brother of Banu Fihr, say: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "By Allah, this worldly life compared to the Hereafter is nothing but like when one of you dips this finger of his"—and Yahya pointed with his index finger—"into the sea; so let him look at what it brings back." And in all their hadiths other than Yahya: "I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say that." And in the hadith of Abu Usamah from al-Mustawrid ibn Shaddad, brother of Banu Fihr, and in his hadith also he said: and Isma'il pointed with the thumb.

'Ubaydullah ibn Sa'id, Abu Bakr ibn Nafi', and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi narrated to us: Aflah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn Rafi', the freed slave of Umm Salamah, narrated to me, saying: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say: "If you live long enough, you are about to see a people who go out in the morning in the displeasure of Allah and return in the evening in His curse, having in their hands things like the tails of oxen."

Ibn Numayr narrated to us: Zayd—meaning Ibn Hubab—narrated to us: Aflah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn Rafi', the freed slave of Umm Salamah, narrated to me, saying: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "If you live long enough, you are about to see a people having in their hands things like the tails of oxen, going out in the morning in the anger of Allah and returning in the evening in the displeasure of Allah."

'Amr an-Naqid, Hasan al-Hulwani, and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me—'Abd said: reported to me, while the other two said: Ya'qub—namely Ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd—narrated to us: My father narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, who said: I heard Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab say: The bahirah is that whose milk was withheld for the idols, so no person was allowed to milk it; and as for the sa'ibah, it was what they used to release for their deities, so nothing would be loaded onto it. And Ibn al-Musayyab said: Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "I saw 'Amr ibn 'Amir al-Khuza'i dragging his intestines in the Fire, and he was the first to institute the practice of dedicating animals to idols (sa'ibah)."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Jarir narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "I saw 'Amr ibn Luhayy ibn Qama'ah ibn Khindif, the forefather of these Banu Ka'b, dragging his intestines in the Fire."
